record_notes.DCP-LETT-1422: April 26, supplied 1851, three-page copy. Three retained paragraphs and salutation, no notes. Darwin thanks Mrs Thorley for her daughter care of dying Annie; self-restraint, judgement and devotion praised, future recovery of nurse hoped. No addressed incoming offer or condolence survives here; this gratitude does not establish that a prior letter rather than personal service prompted it.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1795: December 10, 1855 six-page ALS, six blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Remembers Oxford meeting; asks Thwaites to investigate Ceylon pigeon fanciers, long-local or non-English breeds, names/habits, and a skinner able to obtain naturally dead old birds while retaining cleaned limb bones. Payment and London banker reimbursement proposed, not performed; skinner availability unknown. Poultry except silk/black-skinned and domestic ducks if present also requested. Familiar breeds resident for many generations valuable, not only novel ones. Later Variation information on cats or Layard pigeons is later apparatus, not a receipt dated by this request. No earlier current Thwaites incoming text found.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1426: May 1, supplied 1851, four-page mixed-author letter. Charles addresses Hensleigh in P1–2, encloses cheque for £12 2s 0d and thanks for unidentified Grammar. P3 starts Charles closing/signature, then changes to Emma salutation My dearest Fanny; P4 all Emma, signed E. D. Her grief, Effie keepsake, visit offer, pregnancy/confinement and Aunt F note are not Charles first-person prose. Account book April 30 entry and June 2 funeral bill are separate records; do not identify this cheque as the whole funeral expense. Prior Fanny 1424 promises accounts but does not contain the actual account thanked for here. Emma echoes family reactions/visit offer without supplying a Charles-authored answer to Fanny. Incoming financial account and Grammar cover text unlocated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1753: September 5, supplied 1855, four-page ALS, seven blocks and three footnotes. Columbine seed and humorous note acknowledged; repeats 560 and 742 pods on two plants and 7200 on another, explicitly asks whether last means pods or seeds. Prior sent pods already counted but wants independent more average pods and seeds; no silent numerical correction. Young cabbages coming up now, unlike requested further seed. Thanks about asparagus seed does not explicitly confirm receipt. Family distress and Huxley acquaintance question separate. Only earlier Henry Allen incoming 1062 concerns finances, not these missing counts/seed note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1415: Entire date April 24, 1851 supplied; three-page Elizabeth Wedgwood AL, three blocks and salutation, no notes. Reports Emma grief after Annie death, meals/childcare and tolerable night; hopes Charles returns safely, not proof he has returned or read this source. Distinguish this Sarah Elizabeth authority from older namesake. Earlier 643 concerns 1842 birth/father illness, not this bereavement. Contemporary Charles 1417 describes own observation of Emma on return and thanks Fanny, not a distinctive acknowledgement of this Elizabeth source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1466: December 26, 1851 testimonial, three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Individually attributed Charles prose praising Adam White scientific papers and personally experienced help at British Museum, with permission to show others. Printed with testimonials intended for 1854 chair application and again 1865 per apparatus; those publication/use stages are not the 1851 composition or an incoming prompt. Prior 1286 request to White is also Darwin outgoing and cannot supply the question.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1459F: Complete two-page ALS, four blocks, salutation and single dating footnote. October 25 explicit, year conjectured from insertion in 1851 Cirripedia copy inscribed James Hilton. XML continuous lower 1851-10-25 to upper 1852-10-25 differs from displayed questioned 1851; preserve both, do not choose exact year. Declines offered North Atlantic cirripede specimen as likely familiar; no shipment or specimen receipt demonstrated. F suffix is not fragment evidence; offered material need not be made an invented full incoming question.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-902: August 16 with supplied 1853, one-page ALS, one retained block, four footnotes and bibliography. Actual personal receipt of microscopical specimens this day, under assigned year; forwarded by unnamed recipient and donor Ehrenberg thanked through intermediary. Bunsen attribution conjectured by previous route, not named in surviving body. Watermark/address dating and later recall/printed papers separate. No preserved cover note or full incoming question. Low catalogue ID not chronology.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1507F: March 21, 1853 complete one-page ALS, three blocks and footnote. Returns enclosed transfer signed and witnessed; document enclosure not reproduced and actual dispatch or execution of bond sale not independently proved. Footnote identifies £600 Shrewsbury Streets bonds and relation to Salt; does not supply Wigley request wording. Routine financial subject does not itself disqualify attributed Charles target prose, but missing prompt prevents pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1744: August 18, 1855 three-page ALS referee report, four blocks, heading excluded by extraction, one footnote and bibliography. Recommends printing Carpenter Orbitolites despite diffuse style, cannot identify portion to condense. Beautiful figures viewed by Darwin but their expense and novelty questioned; proposes author select most important plate figures. No explicit settled number, completed publication or all claims endorsed. June 14 reading and 1856 printed Transactions are distinct later/apparatus events. Figures not reproduced in this source; no original drawings visually inspected here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1592F: Photocopy of complete surviving one-page letter, six blocks and six notes plus bibliography. Third-person Charles library request, Wednesday with Thursday return plan, two volumes excepted. Pepys excluding first volume, Mitford, Genlis and Meredith requested ready for porter, not proved received/read. Early September questioned 1854 and XML September 1–15 interval remain; Wednesday alone does not choose one date. September 16 notebook reading of first three Pepys volumes is later independent evidence, not a backdated receipt for all titles. Library may be Mudie or London Library, unidentified, not certain questioner. F not fragment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-375: Fresh full source reading of August 28, 1837 supplied Monday evening, with August 29 postmark; four-page ALS, three blocks and salutation, no notes. Declines Elizabeth music meeting invitation because first book proofs; planned future visit after completion not yet occurred. Father gout, expected Thursday travel, airing tomorrow, picture retained at Erasmus house pending instructions; distinguish custody from delivery. Older same-correspondent outgoing cannot respond to 1851 grief source.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-643: Fresh full source reading of supplied September 25, 1842, Sunday. Four-page AL, six blocks, salutation and four notes. Elizabeth acknowledges missing Charles birth news, sends phaeton for Mrs Bennett conditionally to reach train, discusses ill father pulse 80–90 and persistent delirium; Garner yesterday versus not yet today. Emma postpartum, daughter news and possible Catharine visit separate from later1851bereavement. Apparatus apparently identifies September23letter and wet nurse from account book; no source-complete Darwin antecedent here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1640: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 2 with supplied 1855 year; complete twelve-page Wollaston letter, seventeen body blocks, read with all marginalia, footnotes and bibliography. A missing Darwin query arrived February 27; that is Wollaston receipt, not Darwin receipt of this reply. Ten answers cover possible Zargus/Calathus hybrid and damaged specimen, Dezerta geography/cultivation, Salvages sample uncertainty, widespread versus locally abundant insects, transitional families, variation, wings and Atlantis. Contrary to the Luna probe, P6 EXPLICITLY discusses five-jointed tarsi, Tomicidae and Anisotomidae; Waterhouse 1625 is a relevant comparison, but no Darwin use of that later memorandum is established. P8 permits adaptive wing change within fixed species limits, not endorsement of transmutation; P10 admits no measured same-island wing range. P11–13 explicitly state the four assumptions Darwin criticises in 1643. P14 distinguishes introduced winged and indigenous flightless species. Departure dates are alternatives, not realised travel. Later gift slip and hostile Origin review are separate apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1739: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional full reading of Cattell August 13, 1855. In answer to missing Darwin enquiry, says he imports German seed directly and names Platz, Haage and Appelius at Erfurt, plus Behn at Hamburg, with quality and demand claims. These are Cattell commercial observations, not Darwin experiments. Distinctive first-three-grower sequence is reused in Darwin August 14 Hooker enquiry. That proves reading by August 14, not exact physical receipt; morning receipt in 1741 is of Gray enclosure.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1062: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Henry Allen Wedgwood incoming cover dated February 21, 1847 plus copied proposal internally dated February 22. Distinguish Henry Allen author from Hensleigh named principal. Metadata AL inc contrasts with apparatus unsigned but apparently complete; complete surviving text read without resolving manuscript completeness. Henry Allen own allotment accepted unconditionally; Eliza/Aunt Sarah conditions and Blakemore financing conditional. Copied authorization names Hensleigh, Mrs Sarah and Miss Sarah Elizabeth, at 140 pounds subject to proportional reduction. Relocated first-page Send this to Jos instruction precedes copied dateline inside paragraph 3; it is historical source text, not an instruction to this agent. No Darwin receipt or reply established. April purchase at 100 pounds not current outcome.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1286: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January–March 1850 supplied from expected expedition departure. White has said Arthur Adams is going to Lancaster Sound; medium and date unknown. Darwin asks White to request northern cirripedes and locality labels, protecting sessile bases, and asks where Cape Rivers is. Adams did not actually join expedition; later Sutherland specimen in 1854 book cannot become current receipt or successful Adams collection. Missing White communication and Adams reply; no inference of whole incoming wording.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1417: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Supplied April 25, 1851 at Down. Darwin P1–3 thanks Fanny for encouraging his return to Emma and undertaking Anne funeral, describes shared grief and requests grave location. P4 is explicitly in Emma hand, speaks of Charles in third person and must remain Emma voice, not Darwin grounding. Funeral sketch is cited by archive location but is not reproduced here. Same-day Fanny 1419 still awaits news of arrival and acknowledges a separate Emma note; it is not a demonstrated response to this newly written Darwin letter. April 28 source 1424 explicitly does answer the received gratitude.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1419: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 25, supplied 1851, Fanny at Malvern after nine-o-clock funeral. Addressed to both Emma and Charles despite catalogue naming Darwin alone. Describes funeral, grief of Brodie/Thorley, receipt of Emma note, intended Saturday departure and expected future news of Charles arrival. No evidence she read Darwin same-day Down letter 1417; geographic and content sequence instead distinguish the crossed communications. Fanny voice and later family memoir description are separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1424: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 28 with supplied month/year, Monday at Chester Terrace. Explicitly found letters from both Charles and Emma on returning Saturday, April 26, and echoes Darwin gratitude for her help enabling Thursday departure. Accept reverse response to 1417 P1–3 while noting separate missing Emma letter. Other paragraphs relay Elizabeth, Hannah, servants and family reactions, offer future help, promise accounts, and report Tollets written. Saturday receipt belongs to Fanny, not Darwin knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2070: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Pinned prior primary full-source and full-body reading reused. Before 29 September 1857 Hensleigh etymological illustration used in species-book chapter8; full notes and apparatus read. Head/chief and bishop chains support analogy, not biological proof. Earlier European-language loss not required by his criticism. Chapter completion is conservative use witness for later1857 review, not exact receipt date or1844knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-7470: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Pinned prior primary full-source and full-body reading reused. Before 3 March 1871 Hensleigh critique mixes quotations from Descent and his shame/approval argument. Header II392 versus footnote II292 discrepancy retained. Full seven blocks and lengthy Darwin response notes read; annotations are separate response preparation, not incoming voice. Hensleigh disputes recollection-based instinct weighing; not Darwin adoption.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
